subsystems.name: Front end
subsystems.role: expresses an algorithm as gates acting on qubits.

subsystems.name: Intermediate representation
subsystems.role: a hardware-neutral form the rest of the stack compiles from.
parts: gate-level IR with typed qubit references

subsystems.name: Optimisation and routing
subsystems.role: rewrites the circuit to use fewer and shorter operations, then maps virtual qubits onto real ones.

subsystems.name: Native lowering and pulse control
subsystems.role: turns abstract gates into the physical control signals a machine accepts.
parts: gate decomposition into the native gate set
calibration data for each qubit pair

subsystems.name: Error mitigation and correction
subsystems.role: reduces the effect of noise on results.

buildSteps.title: Fix the abstract interface
buildSteps.detail: Define how an algorithm describes qubits, gates and measurements so that many front ends can target the same stack.

buildSteps.title: Build the hardware-neutral IR
buildSteps.detail: Lower the circuit into a typed intermediate representation, typically an LLVM-based dialect, that can be optimised and reasoned about.

buildSteps.title: Read the device model
buildSteps.detail: Import a machine description: which qubits exist, which pairs can interact, native gates, and timing constraints.

buildSteps.title: Map and route
buildSteps.detail: Because not every qubit is connected to every other, insert swaps or teleportations so interacting qubits become neighbours.

buildSteps.title: Optimise within the constraints
buildSteps.detail: Cancel redundant gates, fuse rotations, and schedule operations so that parallel gates do not conflict in time.

buildSteps.title: Lower to native gates and pulses
buildSteps.detail: Decompose into the machine's native gate set and translate each gate into calibrated control pulses for the drive electronics.

buildSteps.title: Wrap with mitigation
buildSteps.detail: Apply readout correction and noise-scaling or noise-cancelling techniques so that computed expectation values are closer to the ideal.

buildSteps.title: Run and measure
buildSteps.detail: Execute repeated shots, gather statistics, and hand results back to the hybrid classical optimiser that adjusts the next circuit.

buildSteps.title: Validate against simulation and benchmarks
buildSteps.detail: Compare against classical simulators of small circuits and against randomised benchmarking on real hardware.

prerequisites.tech: Working qubit hardware with open control
prerequisites.why: superconducting, trapped-ion, neutral-atom and photonic machines all expose gate and pulse interfaces.
QIR lets front ends, optimisers and hardware backends be developed by different groups.
calibrations drift, so compilers need continuously refreshed hardware models to be accurate.
small circuits can be checked exactly on classical computers, which is how bugs are found.
a fault-tolerant stack needs the decoder to keep up with syndrome measurements in real time.

pathway.milestone: mature circuit compilers and transpilers shipping with cloud hardware backends
pathway.unlocks: researchers can run small noisy circuits without writing machine-level code.

pathway.milestone: pulse-level and calibration-aware compilation as the default
pathway.unlocks: meaningfully lower error rates from the same physical qubits.

pathway.milestone: error mitigation and lightweight correction combined in the runtime
pathway.unlocks: larger circuits whose results are trustworthy enough for chemistry and optimisation problems.

pathway.milestone: real-time decoding integrated with logical-qubit compilers
pathway.unlocks: programming against error-corrected logical qubits rather than physical ones.
